method.auditor: Antigravity CLI (agy), model 'Gemini 3.8 Flash (High)', prompted as a harsh brand strategist

briefs.business: Rounds 1-14: show pitched as AI inside a real operating business (departments, fleets, payroll) vs one-man YouTube channels.
briefs.everyday_plus_business: Rounds 15-24: updated after the 2026-09-22 Google Meet (01:00-01:04). Early episodes cover AI for normal people in everyday life ('make AI not a scary monster for normal people', quick use cases, 'Does AI make you a hermit?'), business later, told by people who run a real company. Fit score measures both.

method.pass_rule: cheesiness >= 7 AND stretch >= 7 AND auditor flag = ok (pun, cliche, forced or generic = reject)
method.collision_rule: WebSearch '"<name>" podcast' for every audit survivor; exact-name collisions with existing shows or AI brands dropped
method.diversity_rule: Revision 2 (lead request): at most 2 payroll/employee names, at most 2 truck/fleet names, at least 4 names that work for everyday AI as well as business, drop Hundred Truck Company (unverifiable fleet size)
method.final_pass: Final 10 re-sent to the auditor under the everyday-plus-business brief for a head-to-head ranking; ranking in podcast-name-options.json follows it
method.banned: roof/shingle/top/overhead puns, AI jammed into words, 'The X Podcast', buzzwords (Unleashed, Disrupt, Future of, Revolution, 2.0, Hacks)

revisions.summary: Rounds 1-14 under the business brief produced 10 finalists; lead flagged too many payroll and truck names.

Rounds 15-24 under the everyday-plus-business brief. Kept 6 (AI With a Payroll, Fleet and Payroll, After the Demo, Blue Collar Compute, More Than Two Trucks, The Automation Yard); added 4 new (Kitchen Table AI, Everyday Operators, Day Job AI, Everyday Company). After the Demo re-passed under the new brief (fit 8), so 5 of 10 cover everyday AI. The other 5 kept names failed the re-audit under the new brief and are offered as business-side options only.

notes: Auditor flagged Everyday Company as close to Everyday Operators; offer one or the other if space is tight. Round 24 tried to replace it with a more distinct everyday name; none passed.
Near-misses worth a human look: 'The Everyday Operator', 'Twenty Trucks Deep', 'Before the Truck Rolls', 'The Second Estimator', 'Workhorse AI', 'Weekday AI', 'Day to Day AI', 'Can It Do That'.
